title: customer-x-incident-timeline-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for Customer X (acct: customer-x, prod region: us-west-2) — internal breadcrumbs and comms draft.

High-level summary:
- On 2026-03-01 ~09:20 PST we started seeing increased 95th/99th latency for text-generation routes for Customer X (route: /v1/generate, model pinned: redwood-llama-70b-8q).
- Errors: intermittent 503s and stream disconnects; also observed per-request token-generation stalls (~>10s per token).
- Customer reported elevated error rate to their SRE at 09:35 PST.
- Mitigation: rolled model fallback to smaller variant (redwood-llama-13b-8q) at 10:05 PST which reduced errors but did not eliminate tail latency.

Timeline (raw notes)
- 2026-03-01 09:12: initial alert from internal monitoring: route /v1/generate 99th latency jumped to 4.2s (baseline ~1.0s).
- 2026-03-01 09:20: customer slack -> reports "sudden timeouts and many partial responses"
- 2026-03-01 09:28: I ssh'd into the serving pool (dedicated pool cust-x-1) to check GPU utilization: nvidia-smi shows 60-80% GPU utilization but CPU on the host at 95% (spikes).
- 2026-03-01 09:32: checked runtime logs for PID 11245 (model loader loop): found repeated lines: "kv-cache miss, falling back to full forward" and occasional GC pauses logged by runtime.
- 2026-03-01 09:40: observed Redis latency spikes on prefix cache (redis://kv-cache-1:6379) — p50 2ms -> p99 250ms.
- 2026-03-01 09:50: attempted graceful restart of one inference worker (svc-custx-worker-3) — no immediate effect on aggregated tail latency.
- 2026-03-01 10:02: rolled policy to route new requests to redwood-llama-13b-8q (smaller model) as a workaround. Error rate dropped by ~60% but tail latency still elevated.
- 2026-03-01 10:20: open ticket with infra: suspected contention on redis prefix/shard.

Commands tried (not exhaustive)
- curl check (simulating API, short prompt):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-70b-8q","input":"Hello"}'
  -> sometimes returns HTTP 503, sometimes returns delayed streaming response.

- runtime log tail (on node):
  sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f | sed -n '1,200p'
  found repeated pattern:
  [2026-03-01T09:31:02Z] WARN kv_cache.lua: cache miss for prefix 0x7a4f
  [2026-03-01T09:31:02Z] INFO runtime.scheduler: falling back to full forward for request req=0x112e4
  [2026-03-01T09:31:03Z] WARN runtime.gc: minor GC pause 180ms

- redis latency check (from pod):
  redis-cli -h kv-cache-1 ping; redis-cli -h kv-cache-1 latency latest
  -> observed high spikes: "peak_usec: 250000" around 09:38

- heap/profile snapshot (quick):
  curl http://127.0.0.1:9001/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-0900.pb
  (uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-dev-dumps/customer-x/heap-0900.pb)

Error snippets copied from runtime logs
- "WARN kv_cache.lua: cache miss for prefix 0x7a4f"
- "INFO runtime.scheduler: falling back to full forward for request req=0x112e4"
- "ERROR stream: write failed: write tcp 10.12.3.45:443->10.0.0.7:52344: write: connection reset by peer"
- "WARN runtime.gc: minor GC pause 180ms"
- "redis: IO error - read tcp 10.1.2.11:6379: i/o timeout"

Hypotheses (brainstorm)
- Hypothesis A (kv-cache contention): Redis prefix shard experienced temporary network/IO spikes causing many cache misses; runtime falls back to full forward which increases CPU/GPU pressure and causes GC and stalls. Evidence: redis latency spikes aligned with kv_cache miss logs.
- Hypothesis B (model-specific kernel path): The 70b quantized execution path has a known edge-case where certain sequence lengths trigger slower kernels on our current CUDA/driver combo — but this would be model-path specific; fallback to 13b helping suggests cache/pressure rather than kernel bug.
- Hypothesis C (host-level resource contention): CPU saturation on host (95%) causing scheduler delays in the runtime leading to tail stalls observed as minor GC pauses.

Immediate next steps (TODO)
- [ ] Get full redis slowlog for the timeframe 09:20-10:10 and correlate with request IDs (ask infra for shard logs). Linked ticket: JIRA-INC-1847.
- [ ] Run targeted simulation: replay a sample of Customer X traffic against a staging pool with 70b model and artificially throttle redis to replicate behavior. (Assigned to Priya)
- [ ] Upload and analyze pprof CPU profiles from affected workers (s3 path above). Priority: get CPU flamegraphs for 09:30 window. (Connor)
- [ ] Confirm network metrics between serving nodes and redis (packet drops, retransmits). Ask infra to look at the ENI in us-west-2b.
- [ ] Draft internal comms to CS/Eng/SRE describing timeline and temporary workaround (see draft below).

Draft internal comms (for review)
Subject: [INC-1847] Customer X - elevated tail latency on /v1/generate (timeline + next steps)

TL;DR: Customer X experienced elevated 95/99 latency and intermittent 503s for text-generation starting ~09:20 PST on 2026-03-01. Immediate mitigation: routed new requests to a smaller model at 10:05 PST which reduced error rate. Current hypothesis: transient kv-cache/redis latency spike causing cache misses and expensive full forwards.

What happened:
- Spike in redis latency caused a surge of kv-cache misses logged by the runtime. Many requests fell back to full forward path (heavier CPU/GPU work) which increased host CPU and triggered minor GC pauses -> tail latency.

Actions taken:
- 10:05 PST: routed Customer X to redwood-llama-13b-8q as a temporary mitigation.
- Collected heap/cpu profiles and pprof dumps; uploaded to s3 for analysis.
- Opened infra ticket to investigate redis shard IO and network path (JIRA-INC-1847).

Next steps:
- Correlate redis slowlog + request ids to identify whether a specific prefix or key range was hot.
- Replay traffic in staging with throttled redis to reproduce and confirm root cause.
- If redis contention is root, consider: re-sharding, client-side request coalescing, or adaptive retry/backoff in runtime to reduce fallbacks.

Quick notes to self:
- Keep Customer X PM/SRE updated every 2 hours until resolved.
- If we see recurrence after redis fix, re-evaluate kernel path hypothesis and collect low-level CUDA logs.

Conversation snippets to include for audit (internal):
- customer slack: "We are seeing partial responses and the UI shows spinning for some responses" (09:35)
- on-call SRE: "There were significant retransmits on ENI usw2b-eni-28 around 09:36" (captured in infra DM)

File refs / dump locations:
- s3://redwood-dev-dumps/customer-x/heap-0900.pb
- s3://redwood-dev-dumps/customer-x/cpu-pprof-0930.pb

Notes end. Will update as infra and Priya/Connor add analysis.

-- Jamie
